**Refined prompt:** Answer whether two articles published with an identical title end up with the same slug in this codebase, grounded in the actual slugify implementation and the storage guarantees around it — short factual answer with citations, plus whatever adjacent risk the code actually carries.

**No.** The slug isn't derived from the title alone, so identical titles don't produce identical slugs.

```ts
// src/article/article.service.ts:201-203
slugify(title: string) {
  return slug(title, {lower: true}) + '-' + (Math.random() * Math.pow(36, 6) | 0).toString(36)
}
```

Called once at create (`article.service.ts:175`), so two people publishing "How I Learned Rust" get `how-i-learned-rust-k2x9fq` and `how-i-learned-rust-3bm0zt`. The suffix is drawn purely from `Math.random()` — the author isn't an input — so "two different people" and "the same person twice" are the identical case.

**Collision odds:** the suffix space is 36⁶ ≈ 2.18×10⁹, so any given pair of same-title articles collides with p ≈ 4.6×10⁻¹⁰. By the birthday bound you'd need on the order of 55,000 articles sharing one title before it's a coin flip. Not a practical concern.

**What is worth knowing, since nothing guards the case:**

1. `slug` is a plain `@Column()` — no unique index (`article.entity.ts:11`, confirmed in `.claude/knowledge/schema.md:31`), and `create()` does no uniqueness query before `save()` (`article.service.ts:170-188`). A duplicate would be accepted silently.
2. If one ever existed, `delete()` is `this.articleRepository.delete({ slug: slug })` (`article.service.ts:198`) — a criteria delete, which removes **every** matching row, not one. `findOne({slug})` on the read paths would return an arbitrary one. So the failure mode isn't "error on publish", it's "one delete takes out both articles."
3. Unrelated to collisions but adjacent: `update()` never re-slugs when the title changes (`article.controller.ts:61` `// Todo: update slug also when title gets changed`), so slugs drift away from titles over time. That's already the more likely source of confusing URLs here.

One quirk in that line, since I read it: `Math.random() * Math.pow(36, 6) | 0` — `36⁶ = 2,176,782,336` exceeds the 2³¹ ceiling of `| 0`, so roughly 1.35% of the time the value wraps negative and `toString(36)` emits a leading `-`, giving slugs like `how-i-learned-rust--zik0zk` with a double hyphen. Cosmetic, doesn't affect uniqueness.
